title: Checkout with retries
brief: Support says some customers were charged twice for one order, mostly when the card processor was slow. Read the checkout code, find out how that can happen, and fix it.

issues.why: A timeout does not mean the charge failed. The retry calls charge() again with no idempotency key, so the processor charges the card a second time. The test gateway does exactly this.
issues.good_fix: Make one key per order (for example the order id) and pass it on every attempt via the three-argument charge(). Keep it stable across retries and across repeated checkout calls.

issues.why: Two requests for the same order both read NEW and both charge. Reading the status and marking PAID are not one atomic step.
issues.good_fix: Claim the order atomically first (compare-and-set NEW to PROCESSING, a lock per order id, or a conditional UPDATE in the database). The key from the first fix also makes the second charge harmless.

issues.why: The empty catch drops the interrupt flag, so a shutdown or a cancelled request keeps retrying.
issues.good_fix: Restore the flag with Thread.currentThread().interrupt() and stop retrying.

extension: Add partial refunds. A refund must be safe to retry too, must not exceed what was charged, and must not break the retry fix.
